os-19-22.alt: Outline of a standing body seen from the front with the rib cage drawn in. Dots mark where ECG electrodes go: one on each wrist, one on each ankle, and six across the chest, two beside the sternum and four curving out to the left under the left breast area.

os-19-23.alt: Top: a regular ECG rhythm strip on grid paper, with a bracket showing that one large square is 5 millimeters and a box spanning 1 second. The tall spikes are four large squares apart. Bottom: an enlargement of two beats, labeling the P wave, the Q, R and S points of the QRS complex, and the T wave, with brackets for the PR interval, the QT interval, the PR segment, the ST segment and the QRS complex.
